name: French Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Sign language; word stress category inapplicable and no prosodic-stress description located

sources.citation: Mertz, Justine; Pagel, Lena; Turco, Giuseppina 2024. Gradiency and categoriality in the prosodic modulation of French Sign Language: A kinematic approach using Electromagnetic Articulography. Proc. Speech Prosody 2024. 6 pp. https://shs.hal.science/halshs-04859474
sources.note: Instrumental (EMA) study of signing-rate/size modulation in LSF; prominence marking mentioned only as future work; no word-stress statement.

sources.citation: Blondel, Marion 2022. Prosodie et langue(s) des signes : un aperçu poétique. Conférence invitée, XXXIVe Journées d'Études sur la Parole (JEP 2022). 14 pp. https://hal.science/hal-03923806
sources.note: Overview of LSF prosody (rhythm, lengthening, pauses, intonation-like non-manuals) mostly in the poetic register. On accentuation it says only that a signer 'peut accentuer tel ou tel mouvement dans un signe, et tel ou tel signe dans son énoncé, notamment pour le mettre en relief' (sec. 2.1), i.e. emphatic/rhythmic prominence; cites Wilbur 1999 on ASL stress (velocity peaks). No lexical stress placement rule for LSF.

sources.citation: Mertz, Justine 2022. Phonological contrast and feature inventories in sign language: a study on French Sign Language (LSF). PhD thesis, Université Paris Cité. 210 pp. https://theses.hal.science/tel-04411808
sources.note: No word-stress statement. Segmental/feature phonology of LSF in Brentari's Prosodic Model; notes (p.3) that movement is the syllable nucleus and 'the lexicon of sign language is thus mainly composed of monosyllabic signs', disyllabic signs being rare; stress/accent placement is never discussed.

sources.citation: Kelepir, Meltem (ed.) 2020. Topics in the Grammar of French Sign Language (LSF). SIGN-HUB Sign Language Grammar Series, 1st ed. 40 pp. Open access (CC BY-NC-SA), https://thesignhub.eu/grammar/lsf
sources.note: Nothing. The PDF reproduces the full SignGram Blueprint ToC (Phonology Part, Ch. 2 Prosody: 2.1.2 Foot, 2.2.1 Prosodic word, 2.3 Intonation) but the only drafted content is on relative clauses/relative pronouns (Hauser 2019); the Prosody chapter is empty in the PDF and on the online platform (tag pages 100-105 return no content).

sources.citation: Catteau, Fanny; Blondel, Marion; Vincent, Coralie 2016. Variation prosodique et traduction poétique (LSF/français) : Que devient la prosodie lorsqu'elle change de canal ? Actes de la conférence conjointe JEP-TALN-RECITAL 2016, vol. 1 (JEP). 10 pp. https://shs.hal.science/halshs-01354719
sources.note: Prosodic contours in LSF poetry and its spoken-French translations; mentions 'accentuation ou emphase' as a prosodic notion in general; no statement on LSF word stress.

sources.citation: Millet, Agnès; Niederberger, Nathalie; Blondel, Marion 2015. French Sign Language. In Jepsen et al. (eds.), Sign Languages of the World: A Comparative Handbook, 273-316. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
